BACKGROUND:I generally purchase visitor’s medical insurance for my parents and in laws when they visit me in the United States once a year, so 4 plan purchases a year.I’ve used a couple of other brokers in the past and have been disappointed in product knowledge and level of service, until I found Insubuy.Since I found about Insubuy from a friend, I’ve been purchasing from them over the past few years.I’ve never had to invoke the after sales service until my mom fractured her arm and we had to use the visitors medical insurance. This is the specific example mentioned below.SPECIFIC EXAMPLE THAT HAS PROMPTED ME TO WRITE THIS REVIEW:The insurance company covered the injury as per the terms of the plan, with the significant exception of the associated physical therapy. You would think that it should be covered if the ER visit was covered as well as the doctor’s visits, even more so if it was in network for everything (I had checked everything out before purchasing the plan, with Insubuy’s help), but it doesn’t seem to work like that.The insurance company stiffed me for about 2900 dollars’ worth of physical therapy, but covered the 3500 dollars of the ER visit and associated CT scan, X-rays, etc, as well as a few hundred dollars’ worth of doctor’s visits.I checked with the provider and it turns out they used the correct billing codes. However, although PT and OT are handled the same way by US insurance companies for US residents, visitors medical insurance chooses to only cover PT (which means getting an actual prosthetic, which only reflects about 10% of the cases).You would think that after an in network doctor takes X-Rays in network and provides PT instructions to an in network PT provider, the associated PT would be covered. Turns out that it’s not, or more accurately, the insurance company chose not to.I contacted Insubuy and they asked me to send over all the associated paperwork (explanation of benefits, claim denials, provider bills and so on). I also discussed the situation with Jagruti and Fallon. Jagruti is on the sales side, she mentioned they represent the customer (as in, me). Lyle helped me fill out the paperwork. Fallon is the insurance claims person and she connected with the insurance company. A couple of weeks later, the insurance company covered it all, subject to the terms of the deductible. This was Fallon going out of her way to help me get a positive outcome and I am very grateful.The reason I’ve excluded the insurance company’s name from this review is because it doesn’t matter. What does matter is the fact that Insubuy (specifically Fallon, Jagruti and Lyle) helped fix a very expensive situation for me. I did read reviews about instances of Insubuy helping customers in similar situations (where the insurance company stiffs the customer), but having experienced it myself is frankly awesome.A US insurance company is unlikely to engage in shenanigans of this sort, for obvious regulatory reasons. However, it seems that providers of visitors medical insurance have greater latitude or perhaps interpretation, of coverage. My only advice to you is to read EVERY word of the benefits agreement. Oh and definitely take the advice provided by the Insubuy sales reps! LOL that goes without saying.PROS OF INSUBUY:• Excellent Product knowledge (they know more about the products they sell, that many of the insurance company benefits representatives themselves……this was weird!)• The representatives I’ve worked with are Russell, Amanda, Lyle and Jagruti. I'm missing some names. I’ve never found any of Insubuy’s reps to not know stuff off the bat; they really do know all the nuances. • Their recommendations were tailored to fit my individual needs. • A good website that actually can price on the spot• They work for the customer, not for the insurance company• Excellent after sales serviceCONS OF INSUBUY:• I really didn’t find any. In general, with any insurance broker, you can usually find a couple of customer service reps who don’t know as much, or the response time is poor, or perhaps they disappear after the product is sold.• However, none of these apply here.• In short, I’m impressed.

I thought of sharing my experience for anyone who plan to buy the Travel Insurance before traveling to US. Just like everyone I too was with the same impression that Travel Insurance is a waste of money as it will try to deny any claim submitted. I was having Safe Travel Insurance Comprehensive which I bought from Insubuy. Due to a viral illness, my relative required a hospitalization for critical care. The hospitalization included 911, Emergency Room and 2 days of hospital stay. I submitted the insurance and hospital submitted the claims to the insurance company. The claims were denied stating it as pre-existing condition. I further submitted appeals on my own and that too got denied for the same reason. Before my second appeal, I reached Insubuy and requested their support. This was after 8 months of this incident. Insubuy without any hesitation engaged their support and a claims specialist. They prepared the appeal which I submitted to the insurance company with required supporting document. The claims got approved without any further questions! It was a huge relief for me as the hospital bill was really high. My 2 cents – If you ever plan to buy a Travel Insurance please buy from Insubuy. Before you purchase the insurance, talk to them and take their advice and buy the right plan. For an unfortunate reason, if an hospitalization happen during the travel, please reach Insubuy and take their advice. Never ever submit claims on your own. Get the help from Insubuy claims specialist and submit the claims or appeals.

The following is a letter I sent to Jewlers Mutual several months ago concerning how a feel about the service the company provided to me. Dear Ms. Finch:     There is a first time for everything. After dealing with insurance companies on my own behalf and on behalf of numerous clients for more than a half of decade, this is the first time I felt moved to express gratitude for the service provided. A stumble that I experienced several months ago and the resulting damage caused to my diamond ring that had been given by my mother to my father many years ago set in motion a chain of events involving Jewlers Mutual, all of which proved to be of great satisfaction to me. First, Mackenzie Clemons handled my claim very efficiently and in all respects most fairly. My father’s ring setting  was retained and fitted with a beautiful diamond that I surrendered for the damaged one. Indeed, that ring is flashing across this key board as I am typing this letter to you. 	However, once I surrendered the damaged diamond my conscience got the better of me; I had abandoned a family heirloom That’s where your colleague, Kay Kostelny,  entered the picture. I reached out to Ms. Clemons who introduced me to Ms. Kostelny as the person suited to assist in reacquiring the diamond. When I expressed to Kay my hope to require the diamond she promised to assist me and well she did. Not only did we arrive at what I considered to be a fair price for something that was essentially priceless to me, but Kay also arranged to have the stone reworked minimizes damage and enhance its beauty and to obtain a GIA appraisal. Talk about going the extra mile!       Kudos, also, to Sean Hawley, who took care of all the details involving removing the damaged ring from the Jewlers Mutual policy, adding the new ring (actually the old ring with the new stone) to the policy, and finally adding the reacquired diamond to the policy.	Here’s the best part of this rather long story. I have two children whom I equally love. Before I took the stumble I struggled with how to leave my family ring to both of them.  The answer is now apparent. One child will get the ring with my father’s setting and the replacement diamond and the other will receive the original diamond in a setting identical to the one my mother had selected for my father many decades ago.	How many people go around bragging about their insurance company? I do.	     Regards, Ronald S
